title: Acute _Streptococcus pneumoniae_ lung infection: Mouse model and characterisation of the immune response.
protocol: Innoculate 10-20 mL Todd-Hewitt broth supplemented with 0.5% yeast extract with S. pneumoniae.
Culture overnight at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.
Subculture into fresh pre-warmed Todd-Hewitt broth with yeast extract at a ratio of 1:50.
Grow to mid-log phase (OD600 = 0.5-0.7) at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.
Collect the bacteria by centrifugation at 3000xg for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the collected bacteria at OD600 = 1.0 in cold PBS/20% glycerol and keep on ice.
Prepare 1 mL aliquots of resuspended bacteria.
Snap freeze aliquots in liquid N₂, keeping a non-frozen control aliquot on ice to assess viability.
Assess stocks for viable CFU counts by plating out serial dilutions of three frozen samples and one non-frozen control sample on blood agar plates.
Incubate the plates for 24 hours at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.
Confirm S. pneumoniae colonies by presence of an α-haemolytic zone and sensitivity to optochin.
Count colonies and calculate stock CFU concentration.
Ensure viability of frozen stocks is >90% compared to the non-frozen control sample.
Maintain virulent stocks by performing in vivo passage every 6-12 months.
Thaw frozen S. pneumoniae stocks and wash twice by centrifugation (5000xg for 5min) in sterile PBS.
Resuspend S. pneumoniae at 4x10^7 CFU/mL in PBS.
Keep the suspension on ice and use for infection within 2 hours of thawing.
Induce anaesthesia in mice by inhalation of 3% isoflurane for 2-3min.
Maintain anaesthesia with 2% isoflurane for up to 6 minutes.
Hold the mouse in a supine position, allowing the head to tilt slightly backwards.
Mix the _S. pneumoniae_ suspension well.
Collect 50 µL of the suspension containing 2x10^6 CFU using a pipette.
Place small droplets of the suspension on the nostrils to allow inhalation by the mouse.
Observe the mouse to confirm inhalation and full recovery from anesthesia, ensuring re-gaining of righting reflex within 1 minute and normal mobility within 3 minutes.
Infect all mice in the study group intranasally with _S. pneumoniae_ as described above.
Prepare serial dilutions of the inoculum after infecting all mice.
Plate the diluted inoculum on blood agar plates to confirm the infection dose.
Record pre-infection body weights of the mice.
Assess animals to ensure they are in good health before infection.
Infect mice intranasally with _S. pneumoniae_ as described above.
Record body weights daily starting at 24 hours post-infection, preferably at the same time every day.
Monitor animals at least three times a day for a period of 10 days post-infection.
Increase monitoring frequency when signs of sickness are observed.
Perform out-of-hours checks if necessary.
Assign clinical scores according to the established scheme.
Cull animals showing more than 25% body weight loss or reaching score 3.
Exclude and cull mice displaying rare clinical signs such as head tilting, loss of balance, or circling immediately.
Collect blood and tissues for analysis upon culling or at study end-point.
Induce a T-independent antibody response by immunizing mice with Pneumovax II.
Immunize mice using one 100 µL dose (0.4 µg) diluted in sterile PBS at a ratio of 1:12.5.
Administer the vaccine via intraperitoneal injection 14 days before infection with S. pneumoniae.
Include a PBS-treated vehicle control group for comparison.
Induce a T-dependent antibody response by immunizing mice with Prevenar 13.
Immunise mice with four 100 μL doses of Prevenar given 14 days apart by intraperitoneal injection.
Include a PBS treated vehicle control group in the immunisation protocol.
Collect serum from pre- and post-immunisation blood samples to assess antibody levels.
Euthanise mice by CO2 inhalation followed by gentle cervical dislocation to confirm death.
Collect blood samples from the abdominal aorta into appropriate containers for analysis.
Create a small opening in the trachea above the larynx using a needle.
Gently inflate the lungs with 1 mL cold PBS using a syringe and 20g IV cannula.
Withdraw the liquid from the lungs after inflation.
Repeat the lung inflation and liquid withdrawal process three times.
Place BAL fluid in a microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Make a small cut in the left atrium.
Gently hold the heart with forceps.
Insert a 25g needle into the right ventricle.
Gently flush through 10mL cold PBS until the lungs appear white.
Collect lungs and spleens into cold PBS.
Keep collected tissues on ice.
Place lungs into Miltenyi C-tubes with 2.5mL dissociation buffer containing enzymes A and D.
Homogenise tissue using the Miltenyi GentleMACS (lung programme 2).
Incubate with the dissociation buffer at 37°C for 45min with intermittent mixing.
Place samples on ice.
Homogenise a second time using the Miltenyi GentleMACS (lung programme 2).
Transfer the homogenate to 15mL tubes.
Wash by centrifugation at 500xg in 10mL cold PBS.
Resuspend the pellet in 3mL of 37.5% isotonic Percoll at room temperature and centrifuge at 650xg for 20 minutes with low acceleration and no brake.
Carefully remove the supernatant containing debris using a pipette.
Wash the cell pellet in PBS.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200-500μL cold PBS.
Homogenise spleens by pushing through 40µm cell strainers.
Rinse the strainers in 2ml PBS.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15ml tube.
Wash once by centrifugation in 5ml cold PBS.
Resuspend cell pellets in red blood cell lysis buffer (2mL per spleen) and incubate for 5min at room temperature.
Quench lysis by adding 10ml cold PBS and collect the cells by centrifugation.
Resuspend the cell pellets in 2-5ml cold PBS.
Collect cells from BAL fluid by centrifugation at 500xg.
Resuspend cells in 200-500µL PBS and keep on ice.
Place the lungs/left lung in a 2 mL Eppendorf microfuge tube containing 1 mL PBS and 3x 3.2 mm stainless steel beads.
Homogenize the tubes using a Bullet Blender at speed 8 for 3 minutes.
Transfer 200 μL of the homogenate into a U-bottom 96 well plate and keep on ice.
Perform 10-fold serial dilutions for spleen and lung homogenates.
Plate out 100 μL samples using ColiRollers or a bacterial spreader on blood agar plates.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 24 hours.
Count S. pneumoniae colonies on plates with 10-300 colonies, recognized by the presence of a green α-hemolytic zone.
Transfer 200 μL samples of spleen and lung single cell suspensions to U-bottom 96 well plates.
Prepare surface antibody master mix containing FC block and viability dye in staining buffer (0.5% BSA in PBS).
Collect samples by centrifugation and resuspend in 50 μL antibody master mix per sample.
Protect the plates from light and incubate at 4°C for 30-40 minutes.
Quench staining by adding 150 μL staining buffer to each plate.
Collect cells by centrifugation and wash once with 200 μL staining buffer.
Fix samples in 50 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Quench fixation by adding 150 µL of staining buffer.
Collect cells by centrifugation and wash twice with 200 µL of staining buffer.
Resuspend samples in 50-100 µL of PBS, add non-fluorescent counting beads, and analyze on a flow cytometer.
Where intracellular staining is required, collect the cells by centrifugation and wash once with an appropriate permeabilization buffer.
Resuspend cells in 50 µL of intracellular antibody master mix in permeabilization buffer.
Protect samples from light and incubate at room temperature for 40 minutes.
Quench staining, wash, resuspend, and analyze cells as described in steps 8-10.

Before analyzing samples by flow cytometry, ensure that the appropriate unstained and single stained compensation controls as well as required fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) or isotype staining controls are prepared.
